{"m": "gpt-4o-mini", "msg": [{"content": "You compare short personal anecdotes by their underlying relational structure - the pattern of intentions, causes, deceptions, reversals, and outcomes among the people involved - NOT by their surface topic, setting, or vocabulary. Two stories can be about totally different situations yet share the same deep structure; two stories can share the same topic yet have opposite structure.", "role": "system"}, {"content": "SITUATION:
My financial advisor knew my company's acquisition would be structured to cancel all unvested stock options—a detail buried in the SEC filing. He didn't tell me because he 'didn't want to cause panic before the deal closed.' I could have exercised early or negotiated retention. Instead I lost three years of equity compensation while he preserved his 'fiduciary calm.'

CANDIDATE A:
My financial advisor saw warning signs about my company's stability and immediately scheduled a meeting to discuss diversification options. I didn't want to hear it, but his insistence helped me rebalance before the stock dropped.

CANDIDATE B:
My mechanic noticed my brake lines were corroding but didn't mention it because I 'seemed stressed about money.' He planned to address it at my next service. I rear-ended another car a week later. His protection cost me my clean driving record and raised my insurance for years.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:33"}
content: {"choice": "B", "reason": "Both stories involve a professional withholding critical information from a client due to a misguided intention to protect them, resulting in negative consequences."}
